position_authority: Single Python process Positions current state; SQLite generation/owned-location CAS at batch flush
durability_barriers: own haven-bag entry: outside position only
shutdown before and after draining workers

health_tick.changed_hp: Re-read session/HP/baseline under BEGIN IMMEDIATE; compare expected HP; update HP and persisted last_ms only
health_tick.fraction_baseline: initial_hp and started_ms unchanged across ticks
health_tick.clock: Persistent highwater last applied change, plus volatile process observation highwater for skipped ticks

failure_policy.sqlite_failure: Pending positions remain authoritative and dirty; lifecycle does not delete lease or exit until flush succeeds
failure_policy.stale_generation: Evicted after SQLite lease check; cannot update replacement character state; reported explicitly
failure_policy.crash_without_external_journal: May lose latest unflushed interval, unlike graceful shutdown
failure_policy.multi_process: Current LIVE lease and Positions lock are process-local. Redis payload mirroring alone does not make multiple writers safe.

redis_scaling_requirements: Use atomic compare-generation ownership/fencing for movement writes and lease refresh
Version each buffered snapshot and CAS delete only acknowledged versions after SQLite commit
Recovery validates persistent SQLite lease/account/character and baseline location before applying
A new login must fence all old process owners, not merely replace its local LIVE entry
Maintain per-character single writer or distribute ownership explicitly; retain SQLite CAS as final guard
If Redis is durability authority, configure persistence and test crash recovery; optional lossy cache is a different policy
